key_insight: The paper shows that Bell nonlocality can be made significantly more robust by encoding it in logical qubits using quantum error-correction codes, rather than relying on fragile physical qubits.
engineering_relevance: This improves the practicality of device-independent quantum communication and quantum networks by relaxing noise requirements for secure protocols such as DI-QKD.
method: Constructs a general logical Bell inequality within stabilizer-code subspaces.
Analyzes logical nonlocality under decoherence using repetition codes [[3,1,1]] and [[7,1,1]].
Presents an implementation circuit for a logical Bell test based on the [[3,1,1]] code.
evidence_signal: Under a bit-flip error model, the fidelity threshold for violating the logical Bell inequality drops from 82.8% to 73.10% and 66.35%, while the DI-QKD bit-flip noise threshold rises from 10.64% to 14.42% and 23.36% for the [[3,1,1]] and [[7,1,1]] codes, respectively.
watch_item: The reported robustness is demonstrated for repetition-code-based, bit-flip-noise scenarios, so broader performance in realistic multi-error and hardware-specific settings still needs validation.
paper_title: Robust logical Bell nonlocality based on quantum error correction codes
